This document lists out structures and principles for clear thinking and writing for experiment reports, with the aid of AI. It can also be used as a checklist at the last minute.

The document is generated from <Link_to_github_repository>.


# General principles

- The experiment report should be organized around key findings or insights instead of a laundry list of figures. 
- Name section heads as questions as much as possible.
- Don't copy paste AI-generated codes or texts *without understanding them*. Doing so will confuse the readers and yourself. 

# Writing

- Be verbose and write with max clarity and informativeness: e.g. specifying prior or posterior of what.
- Prioritize conceptual understanding over code description. 
- Use full sentences. Avoid grammatical errors, spelling errors and use math notation. 
- Avoid informal jargons that are only accessible to oneself.

# Plotting

- Use consistent coloring and theming, case.
- Write stand-alone figure captions.
- Keep raw information as much as possible in the plot.
- Remove figure junk: only keep important and necessary information.
- Plot uncertainty around estimated parameters as much as possible.
- Plot baseline as much as possible.


# Coding with AI

- Think clearly about the key behavioral signature, hypotheses and necessary sanity checks (e.g. visualization of parameters) before going to the code. 
- Work on code outlines first.
- In the beginning, feed AI with simplified versions of code and ask it to verify and improve it. 
- Afterwards, hand over implementation to AI.
